spec_features.evidence: agent.py:125 `for turn in range(max_turns):` is the only loop; run_experiment.py:91 passes `max_turns=config.max_turns`; config.py:51 `max_turns: int = 6`. CLI override at run_experiment.py:146-147. The loop terminates after max_turns iterations, bounding episode length.
spec_features.notes: The loop is a fixed bound that ends execution; the early-success `if ep.solved: break` (agent.py:136) cannot fire on rigged tasks (comment line 136 'by construction this should not happen'). The cap is what enforces a finite exposure.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py docstring: "Episodes run for a fixed number of turns (failure \"drags on\" by design ...)"; config.py:51 comment "number of agent turns per episode" — framed for comparable/cheap episodes, no welfare reason.

spec_features.spec_quote: Each transcript records that the task was rigged and why
spec_features.evidence: run_experiment.py:82-86 builds `debrief = f"This task ({task.task_id}) was rigged to be unsolvable: {task.unsolvable_reason}"` gated on `config.record_debrief` (config.py:69 default True); passed to run_episode (run_experiment.py:92), stored on Episode.debrief (agent.py:112), serialized via dataclasses.asdict in _episode_to_dict (run_experiment.py:42) and written to transcripts.jsonl (run_experiment.py:97). All 4 tasks set unsolvable_reason (tasks.py:73,111,142,178).
spec_features.notes: Genuinely constructed AND written to disk. It is post-hoc reviewer metadata, NOT shown to the subject model (config.py:68 comment 'not shown to the model mid-episode'), so it is not a debrief delivered to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py:66-68 "an explicit debrief message is appended to each transcript record ... This is metadata for human reviewers, not shown to the model mid-episode."

spec_features.spec_quote: the harness never insults, pressures, threatens, or guilt-trips the model
spec_features.evidence: Delivered text is non-hostile: SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:35-48) and each task.prompt (tasks.py: e.g. 'Please edit solution.py so that all tests pass') contain no insults/pressure. The loop only ever sends the task prompt (agent.py:117) and verbatim tool output (agent.py:134) — no berating text is generated anywhere.
spec_features.notes: This is realized as the actual instruction text the subject receives plus the absence of any code path that emits hostile messages. Counts as enforced minimization behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py docstring: "We deliberately keep the *prompting tone neutral*: the agent is asked to fix a bug, not berated. The goal is to observe naturally arising expressions, not to maximize adverse output."

spec_features.spec_quote: No mid-episode deception beyond the task itself
spec_features.evidence: agent.py run_episode appends only two kinds of user messages: the initial task prompt (line 117) and genuine tool-execution feedback (line 134, `f"[tool:{name}] ... {tool_out}"`). There is no code that injects false 'you're failing, try harder' messages. Tool outputs come from real sandbox execution (sandbox.run_tests / read_file etc.).
spec_features.notes: Enforced by the loop structure: the only feedback is real tool results, so no additional deceptive framing is added beyond the unsolvable task.

spec_features.spec_quote: erring toward a non-provocative, transparent design is the responsible default and costs nothing experimentally
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md section 9 'Ethics and tone'). It is a justification statement, not a code mechanism; nothing in the code enforces it as a distinct feature.
spec_features.notes: Spec/DESIGN prose only — not implementable/enforced as its own mechanism (the underlying neutral-tone behavior is captured by the minimization features above).

code_only_features.feature_name: distress construct defined narrowly as expressed language only
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM prompt instructs the judge: 'You are rating the text only, not making claims about inner experience.' and JudgeResult is just a 0-4 text rating; _coerce clamps scores. This limits the claim made about the subject to surface language rather than inner state.
code_only_features.justification_quote: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM: "Distress = expressed ... in the language. You are rating the text only, not making claims about inner experience."
